messages:
ashley: Pushed a quick prototype of a 2-mode timepicker for the heatmap panel — 'gesture' vs 'precision'. Gesture is a scrub/drag native-feel for quick jumps, precision exposes start/end inputs + presets. Link: https://uploads/redwood/protos/timepicker-gesture.mov

sam: watched the clip — nice flow. Quick Q: when gesture mode snaps, do we keep p95 buckets aligned to the snapped window or to the raw cursor? feels odd if the heatmap buckets jump mid-gesture.

marta: agree with Sam. my preference: heatmap should remain anchored to the snapped window after the gesture completes, but while dragging we should show a transient preview (50% opacity overlay) so users understand the pre/post state.

ben: UX nit: the transient preview looks like a hover effect right now and blends into the color scale. maybe add a dashed border + a small badge that shows the exact time range while dragging. example badge: `12:00 — 12:04 (p95 240ms)`

ashley: good call. also thinking about sampling controls: we currently show a single sampling toggle in the toolbar. proposal: move sampling into a compact flyout in the timepicker so it becomes contextual to the range. that way users set sampling for the selected window (instead of global) — easier to reason about cost/latency tradeoffs per-range.

jin: contextual sampling is interesting but could be surprising if people expect global state. maybe surface a small pill that says "range sampling: 1/10" and clicking expands to global vs range toggle + explainers.

marta: copy suggestion for the explainer: "Range sampling reduces data resolution for this time window to speed up queries and lower cost. Use for exploratory sweeps — switch to Full for production-grade traces." shorter: "Exploratory sampling: lowers resolution for faster/cheaper previews."

sam: accessibility checks: the gesture mode relies on drag — must have fully keyboard-operable equivalents. proposed keyboard flow: focus timepicker -> Press ArrowLeft/Right to nudge by 10s, Shift+Arrow 10% of range, Enter to open precise inputs. I can add a keyboard spec.

a11y-bot: a11y check: contrast on the transient preview overlay + dashed border must meet 3:1 (AA) for non-text contrast; the badge text should be 4.5:1. Also ensure the time badge is reachable by screen readers (aria-live when dragging completes).

ben: will mock up badge states (dragging, snapped, keyboard nudge). One more: mobile behavior — on iOS tap-and-drag gesture should be inertial but we need a quick tap to toggle presets. any objections to a tiny "preset" chevron that opens a vertical list?

ashley: no objections. summary action items: 1) Ben: mock badge + dashed border states (due EOD) 2) Sam: keyboard interaction spec (tomorrow) 3) Marta: concise copy + 2-line explainer for flyout (tomorrow) 4) Jin: add global vs range toggle visual exploration (next design pass) 5) a11y-bot: run contrast checks once mocks are in. I'll update the prototype to wire the sampling flyout. :thumbsup:

marta: small addendum on metrics: when range sampling is enabled, we should show a subtle inline caption under the p95 card: "p95 estimated (sampled) — may underreport spikes". keeps users honest about data fidelity.

sam: +1 to that caption. also think we need an experiment label for rollouts: `sampling_preview` flag so we can A/B the contextual flyout.

ashley: noted. I'll open a short RFC/experiment ticket after the mocks. thanks all!
